gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many hours of three-camera footage each pick keeps on a card before loop recording overwrites it. Using DashCamTalk's per-channel bitrates, a 256 GB card holds about 10.2 h on the Vantrue N4 Pro S, 7.4 h on the 70mai T800 and 4.8 h on the VIOFO A329S 3CH.
standout_why: I checked four of the pages ChatGPT cited. Product Bible's 3-channel page (read 2026-11-21) gives no bitrate and no per-card recording time. It says only that 'three cameras fill a card faster than one or two'. DashCamTalk's best-dash-cams page has no bitrates, hours per card or storage figures. Its only storage line is the A329S's 'external SSD up to 4TB'. Digital Camera World's A329S review has no bitrates and no hours per card. Vortexradar returned HTTP 403, so I couldn't check it. DashCamTalk's separate model pages, which ChatGPT did not get, list bitrates for each channel, but none of them adds the channels together or turns the total into hours per card. The only hours figure I found is Vantrue's own claim of more than 37 h on a 1 TB card for the N4 Pro S. That claim appears in The Weekly Driver, which was not among ChatGPT's results.
decides: This supports the N4 Pro S as the value pick for drivers who need long footage history, such as rideshare shifts or days between offloads. On the same 256 GB card it keeps about 2.1 times as many hours as the A329S 3CH (10.2 h against 4.8 h). It also takes microSD cards up to 1 TB, about 40 h, while the T800 stops at 512 GB, about 14.8 h. It does not knock out the A329S as the image-quality pick. The A329S's higher bitrate is what produces its extra detail, and recording to an external 4 TB SSD would give it about 75 h. The page must say that a lower bitrate is a storage advantage, not a sharper picture. The N4S figure is the weakest of the four, because the data sheet's identical 14.8 Mbps for every camera looks like a repeated value.

findings.label: Bitrate for each channel, 3-channel mode
findings.value: Front 2160p30 at 32 Mbps; cabin 1080p30 at 9.8 Mbps; rear 1440p30 at 14 Mbps
findings.note: DashCamTalk calls these average bitrates. The page is dated December 21, 2025 and shows prices updated 2026-11-21.

findings.label: Hours of 3-channel footage per card (derived)
findings.value: About 25.1 GB per hour, which is about 10.2 h on 256 GB and about 39.8 h on 1 TB
findings.note: (32+9.8+14) Mbps = 55.8 Mbps; 55.8 × 0.45 = 25.1 GB/h (Mbps × 3600 s ÷ 8 ÷ 1000); 256/25.1 = 10.2 h; 1000/25.1 = 39.8 h. This matches Vantrue's own claim of 37+ h on 1 TB (next finding).

findings.label: Vantrue's claimed recording time on 1 TB
findings.value: More than 37 hours with all three cameras recording
findings.source_title: How Vantrue's S1 Pro Max, N4S, N4 Pro S and N5S Dash Cams Differ (Michael Kahn, The Weekly Driver, 2026-10-06)
findings.note: Michael Kahn reports this as Vantrue's claim from Vantrue's Amazon listing and vantrue.com. I did not find the figure on the vantrue.com product page itself. 1000 GB ÷ 37 h = 27 GB/h, which implies about 60 Mbps in total, close to DashCamTalk's 55.8 Mbps.

findings.label: Maximum microSD, power storage, GPS, parking mode
findings.value: microSD up to 1 TB; supercapacitor; built-in GPS; 24/7 parking mode needs a hardwire kit (VP03) sold separately
findings.note: The page shows a sale price of $279.99 (regular $469.99). WebFetch also read 'Sold Out - Notify me when it's available', while the store's product data on the same day said available: true. Check stock before publishing. I did not find a price for the VP03 kit on its own; it appears only inside bundles, such as N4 Pro S + VP03 + 256 GB card + CPL + remote at $428.99.

findings.label: Bitrate for each channel
findings.value: Front 2160p at 65 Mbps; rear 1440p30 at 27 Mbps; interior 1440p30 at 27 Mbps
findings.note: DashCamTalk gives the front 65 Mbps at 60 fps. Digital Camera World's review says the front drops to 4K30 when the interior camera is in use, so the true 3-channel front bitrate may be lower. Treat the hours below as a lower bound.

findings.label: Hours of 3-channel footage per card (derived)
findings.value: About 53.6 GB per hour, which is about 4.8 h on 256 GB, about 9.6 h on 512 GB and about 75 h on a 4 TB SSD
findings.note: (65+27+27) Mbps = 119 Mbps; 119 × 0.45 = 53.6 GB/h; 256/53.6 = 4.8 h; 512/53.6 = 9.6 h; 4000/53.6 = 74.6 h. Digital Camera World's review supports the 4 TB SSD figure: https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/cameras/dash-cams/viofo-a329s-3ch-review-a-flagship-three-channel-dash-cam-for-full-coverage (read 2026-11-21).

findings.label: Frame rate for each channel with all three recording
findings.value: Front 4K30 when the interior camera is in use (4K60 without it); rear and interior 2K30
findings.source_title: Viofo A329S 3CH review: A flagship three-channel dash cam for full coverage – Digital Camera World
findings.note: Digital Camera World's text: 'The forward facing camera records 4K at 30 fps, or 60 fps when the interior camera isn't in use.' It also says parking mode needs hardwiring.

findings.label: Bitrate for each channel
findings.value: Front 2160p30 at 32 Mbps; rear 2160p30 at 32 Mbps; cabin 1080p30 at 13 Mbps
findings.note: The same page lists: maximum card 512 GB; supercapacitor; GPS built in; parking mode needs a 70mai hardwire kit (UP03, or UP04/UP05 for 4G); parking mode is not buffered.

findings.label: Hours of 3-channel footage per card (derived)
findings.value: About 34.7 GB per hour, which is about 7.4 h on 256 GB and about 14.8 h on its 512 GB maximum

findings.label: Bitrate for each channel, and hours per card (derived)
findings.value: 14.8 Mbps per camera, so 44.4 Mbps in total: about 20.0 GB/h, about 12.8 h on 256 GB and about 50 h on 1 TB
findings.note: 14.8 × 3 = 44.4 Mbps; 44.4 × 0.45 = 20.0 GB/h; 256/20 = 12.8 h; 1000/20 = 50 h. Weak input: the data sheet gives the same 14.8 Mbps for all three cameras and conflicts with its own review's front resolution (1944p against 1440p), so this figure may be copied rather than measured. Maximum card 1 TB; capacitor; GPS.

findings.label: Same 256 GB card: N4 Pro S against A329S 3CH
findings.value: About 2.1 times as many hours (10.2 h against 4.8 h)
findings.source_title: Vantrue N4 Pro S – DashCamTalk; VIOFO A329S – DashCamTalk
findings.note: 53.6 GB/h ÷ 25.1 GB/h = 2.13. A lower bitrate saves storage but does not make a sharper picture; the page must say so.
